stem:
Inder wants a fair comparison of two household liquids using one prepared red-rose extract as the indicator.

Which plan makes that comparison fair?

options.text: Use the same rose extract for both, add comparable amounts of each liquid with a dropper, and record the final colour for each sample.
Use one drop of sample A and ten drops of sample B; the test is still fair if the indicator is the same and both final colours are written down.
If both samples can later be labelled acid or base, the comparison must have been fair no matter how it was done.
He also keeps a separate turmeric-paper demo for a different lesson; that separate demo makes today's rose-extract comparison unfair.

teacher.key_rationale: Fairness needs the same indicator, comparable amounts, and recorded final colours in the comparison being judged. Unequal drops omit the amount condition; inferring fairness from later labels reverses the relation; blaming an unrelated separate demo mis-scopes the fairness rule.
